title: Rodrigues SO(3) exponential, left Jacobian, and Gallego-Yezzi rotation derivative as one trigonometric object
expression_sketch:
v in R^3, theta = ||v||, bar_v = v/theta for theta != 0, K = [v]_x the 3x3 skew matrix. Euler-Rodrigues (Murray-Li-Sastry (2.14); Gallego-Yezzi (1),(5)):
  R(v) = exp(K) = I + (sin(theta)/theta) K + (1-cos(theta))/theta**2 K**2
       = I + sinc(theta) K + (1/2) sinc(theta/2)**2 K**2,
with entire continuation R(0)=I. Left Jacobian / dexp on so(3) (Chirikjian; Barfoot; Iserles et al.):
  J_L(v) = I + (1-cos(theta))/theta**2 K + (theta-sin(theta))/theta**3 K**2,
  J_L(0)=I, and d/dt |_{0} exp(K + t [w]_x) corresponds to R * [J_R w]_x (right convention) or [J_L w]_x * R (left).
Gallego-Yezzi Result 1 (compact derivative of a rotated point, u independent of v):
  d(R(v) u)/dv = -R [u]_x * (v v^T + (R^T - I) [v]_x) / ||v||**2   (theta != 0),
limit v->0 equals -[u]_x, matching the generators [e_i]_x. Result 2:
  dR/dv_i = (v_i K + [v x (I-R) e_i]_x) / ||v||**2 * R.
Coefficient confluence: (1-cos(theta))/theta**2 -> 1/2, (theta-sin(theta))/theta**3 -> 1/6, sin(theta)/theta -> 1.
latent_structure: One trigonometric germ (sinc and its even companions (1-cos)/theta^2, (theta-sin)/theta^3) of a single 3-vector v reconstructs the group exponential, the logarithm chart, the left Jacobian dexp, and the Euclidean derivative dR/dv. The theta=0 formulae are not separate programs: they are the entire continuation of the same germ (piecewise unification of the singular Gallego writing with the generator writing).

function_domains.exp: matrix exponential on so(3); here given in closed form by Rodrigues, entire in the entries of K
function_domains.R: SO(3)-valued; R^T R = I and det(R)=1

nonzero_conditions.statement: Gallego-Yezzi (8)-(9) and the Rodrigues quotients are written for theta = ||v|| != 0; the theta=0 members are the separate generator / identity formulae
nonzero_conditions.label: DECLARED
nonzero_conditions.source: Gallego and Yezzi, J. Math. Imaging Vision 51 (2015) 378-384, Result 1 eq. (8) and Result 2 eq. (9), arXiv:1312.0788; Murray, Li and Sastry, A Mathematical Introduction to Robotic Manipulation, CRC 1994, pp. 28-33

positivity_conditions.statement: theta = ||v|| is the Euclidean norm, hence theta >= 0
positivity_conditions.label: DECLARED

analytic_domains.statement: The maps theta |-> sin(theta)/theta, (1-cos(theta))/theta**2, (theta-sin(theta))/theta**3 extend to entire functions on C (Taylor: 1 - theta**2/6 + ..., 1/2 - theta**2/24 + ..., 1/6 - theta**2/120 + ...)
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: Standard Taylor series of sin and cos; Rodrigues formula as the closed form of exp:K -> SO(3) (Murray-Li-Sastry; Gallego-Yezzi (5))

analytic_domains.statement: The exponential map so(3)->SO(3) is surjective; a global chart may restrict to the closed ball ||v|| <= pi (principal logarithm)
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: Gallego-Yezzi, Sec. 2: 'kvk <= pi'; Murray-Li-Sastry, exponential coordinates

branch_conventions: Real trigonometric functions of a real theta >= 0; no complex principal Log.
At theta=0 the axis bar_v is arbitrary (Gallego-Yezzi: 'bar v can be chosen arbitrarily').
Principal rotation: theta in [0, pi] for the inverse (log) chart; the forward Rodrigues formula is valid for all real theta.

limit_domains.statement: v -> 0 in R^3 (equivalently theta -> 0+) is the unrestricted real limit used to recover generators dR/dv_i |_{0} = [e_i]_x
limit_domains.label: DECLARED
limit_domains.source: Gallego-Yezzi, Sec. 3.3 Derivative identity, display (6) and the limit of (9)

source_provenance: Gallego and Yezzi, J. Math. Imaging Vision 51 (2015) 378-384, Results 1-2, eqs. (1),(5),(8),(9)
Murray, Li, Sastry, A Mathematical Introduction to Robotic Manipulation, CRC 1994, Euler-Rodrigues formula

derived_conditions.statement: Entire continuation of the three coefficient germs unifies the theta != 0 Gallego/Rodrigues writings with the identity/generator writings at 0
derived_conditions.label: DERIVED
derived_conditions.source: Taylor series of sin, cos; Gallego-Yezzi Sec. 3.3 limit of (9) equals (6)

derived_conditions.statement: (1-cos(theta))/theta**2 = (1/2)*sinc(theta/2)**2 as an identity of entire functions
derived_conditions.label: DERIVED

public_source: Gallego and Yezzi, A compact formula for the derivative of a 3-D rotation in exponential coordinates, J. Math. Imaging Vision 51 (2015) 378-384, doi:10.1007/s10851-014-0528-x, arXiv:1312.0788; Murray, Li and Sastry, A Mathematical Introduction to Robotic Manipulation, CRC 1994 (Rodrigues); Iserles et al., Acta Numerica 9 (2000) (dexp); Barfoot, State Estimation for Robotics, CUP 2017 (left Jacobian).
why_not_cse_lgg: CSE will not invent the skew-symmetric hat map or unify the 1/theta**2 Gallego formula with the generator formula at the identity. LGG has no SO(3) exponential constructor. Distinct from the general Van Loan Duhamel integral for L_exp: here the Frechet derivative on so(3) collapses to a closed trigonometric polynomial in K.
proposer_leak_risk: Hide: Rodrigues, Gallego, Yezzi, SO(3), left Jacobian, dexp, sinc, Lie algebra, generators. Show unlabeled 3x3 trigonometric polynomials in a skew matrix K and the two writings (theta != 0 quotient vs theta=0 generators) as catalog members.
notes: SciML role: autodiff of rotation parameters in robotics/vision/LieTorch; closed-form sensitivity of expm on so(3). Catalog: G0001=R(v) via Rodrigues; G0002=I at v=0; G0003=d(Ru)/dv Gallego writing; G0004=-[u]_x at v=0; G0005=(sin(theta)/theta); G0006=1. Operators: VALUE, LINEAR_COMBINATION of powers of K, piecewise unification at the repeated node theta=0. NOT Van Loan 2-block. NOT adjoint-linear.
